Pool protected analysis-catalog frames from their signed components

Source: R/privacy_protected.R
dot-pool_protected_release_frames.Rd

dsOMOP 2.10.3 protected catalog releases carry a dsomop_release payload: per owner and stratum the signed noisy person total, histogram cells reconciled to that total, bounded lattice moments, or person-time status and time. Compatible sites (same entry, owners, strata, cells, grids, bounds, caps and allocations) are pooled by summing the signed components; every pooled view is derived once (person totals projected top-down, cells onto their stratum, moments onto their feasible set). Standard and protected frames are never mixed, nothing is pooled across incompatible grids, and every site must be a distinct logical source: two connections to one logical node are refused instead of being counted twice.

Usage

.pool_protected_release_frames(per_site, policy = "strict", columns = NULL)

Arguments

per_site

Named list of released frames.

policy

"strict" or "pooled_only_ok" (record-weighted strata present on only some servers).

columns

The entry's contracted columns (record-weighted schema).

Value

List: result (one row per owner, stratum and interaction view with the pooled persons, mean, SD, quantiles, events and time where defined; the pooled cells as attribute cells) and warnings.

Details

Complete person-time hierarchies are summed and projected from the root down; public view masks select sums of those projected nodes. Nested Achilles histograms use the parent's protected cells as their second margin. First-event and capped recurrent event-time hierarchies project their signed A/B/C nodes from the person or event total down before selecting day, month or year views. Recurrent persons use a separate complete interval-presence vector for distinct contributors among the same K-capped occurrences. Its versioned radial projection enforces public feasibility; retreat toward the event-mass anchor can add bias. Coarse person counts are selected directly, never summed from fine bins.

Record-weighted releases (family RM) are pooled per stratum by .pool_protected_record_moments. Exit-time x status cells of a grouped-time Cox release (family C8) are summed and projected onto their pooled C6 event/non-event parents. Interaction C6/C8 exports retain the complete signed atomic family, projected before view coarsening; supplemental rows and cells retain family and view identifiers. C8 uses finite IPF with a feasible margin repair, not an exact KL/L2 claim. Cox cells are never refitted; the event-weighted q x exposure cells of an SCCS release (w) are not pooled (only its case total).
